title: Law to place financial literacy advisors in senior centers
summary: This bill would require the Department for the Aging to assign at least one financial literacy advisor to each older adult center for a minimum of 20 hours per month. Advisors would give seniors general information on financial planning, end-of-life preparation, tax preparation and common scams, plus referrals to specialized providers and City agencies. The Commissioner would also have to set qualifications and create a training program for these advisors, and the law would take effect 120 days after passage.
